title: You Probably Don't Need Your Own Chain: Evidence From Dissolving One at Scale
description:
The appchain thesis is unwinding. Noble rebuilt as a sovereign L1. Sei deleted CosmWasm and kept its chain. We went furthest — dissolved the chain entirely and moved a network serving 100+ chains onto contracts, while it kept serving traffic.

Your own chain buys consensus-level primitives. It also costs a validator set, a token to defend, and governance to run. Almost nobody audits which side of that ledger their guarantees sit on. We did, mechanism by mechanism.

Chain specs got strictly better: an on-chain hash over off-chain content, verifiable by anyone.

Stake-weighted random pairing moved from consensus to the client, forced by gas and the 256-block BLOCKHASH limit. We show why the guarantee survives, and what you must verify for it to hold.

Dual staking — bonding to a validator and a provider at once — has no analogue without a validator set. We show what replaced it.

You leave with the audit: a repeatable method for deciding whether your protocol needs a chain.
